profile.reading: Per DartPoints own site, this Asheville, North Carolina facility (AVL01) sits at the Biltmore Park Technology Center. The data hall totals 11,200 square feet with 296 kW of critical IT load and 1.5 MW of utility power backed by 2,050 kW of generator capacity and 975 kW of UPS capacity, cooled by 330 ton N+1 capacity units. The site is AICPA SOC compliant and offers 7 network providers across 5 fiber entries.

reading.body:
DartPoints Asheville in Asheville, North Carolina, publishes 1.5 MW of IT capacity, operated by .

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 150 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 38 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DartPoints Asheville. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

North Carolina has 6 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 5 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.47 MW. DartPoints Asheville contributes 1.5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
